evidence.V1: Reads as a stump only from three-quarter/top thanks to the ringed cut face; front and silhouette are a featureless trapezoid that could be a lampshade or bucket.
evidence.V2: Big trunk plus ringed top; the three roots are flat wedges that do not form a medium tier, and there is no small detail (bark cracks, chips, moss).
evidence.V3: Primitive construction: a flared frustum with three flat triangular flanges for roots; the roots read as sheets, not rounded flaring roots.
evidence.V4: Top rim has a soft lip, but the base flange edge is a thin hard step and root wedges end in sharp points; inconsistent.
evidence.V5: Body shows smeared light streaks and a bright blotch on the left (front view), and the root flange bottom edge is jagged in the roots close-up; minor.
evidence.V6: Disciplined: bark brown in 2-3 values with cream/tan end-grain rings; birch and walnut colourways keep structure.
evidence.V7: 440 tris vs medium target 2000, well under (arguably too few for round roots).
evidence.V8: One vertex-colour material and kit palette, but organic form is not a convincing fused smooth shell; flat flanges clash with the kit's rounded stylised wood.
evidence.V9: Studio line correct: anchored, Hull collision, CanTouch off, white colour, origin bottom-centre; gates A1-A18 pass, no cross-shell overlaps.

artifacts: smeared shading streaks/blotch on trunk side (front view)
jagged thin step along the root flange bottom edge (roots close-up)
top_fixes: Rebuild roots as 3-5 rounded, tapering root lobes that bulge out and dip into the ground instead of flat flanges
Add a medium/small tier: bark ridges or cracks, a chipped/uneven cut rim, a small stub or moss patch
Spend more of the budget on segments so the trunk and roots read round and shading is clean
